page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 64 GB of RAM, providing a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio of 4 GB per core. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes L1d, L2, and L3 cache sizes of 32 KB, 0.5 MB, and 32 MB respectively. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the n2d-standard-16 delivers strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2674.77 in stress-ng single-core tests, which places it in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 21390.8 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9335.0. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 93.7 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 48.12 GB/sec for large block write operations. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 277.2 tokens/sec, while prompt processing for the same model averages 921.68 tokens/sec.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the n2d-standard-16 is aligned with its mid-range general-purpose profile, offering a balanced allocation of compute and memory resources without the premium cost of specialized hardware. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and GPU acceleration represents a clear tradeoff, making it unsuitable for heavy storage-bound databases or large-scale deep learning training. The instance is suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate multi-threaded decompression tasks.
